# Athena Code

> Athena Code is an open-source terminal AI coding agent with persistent local
> memory, automatic context recall, and searchable history across coding
> sessions.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/luckeyfaraday/athena-code

## Core facts

- Athena Code is a memory-focused fork of OpenCode.
- It is an independent project, not an official OpenCode distribution.
- It adds durable global and project memory, frozen per-session context,
  per-turn relevant recall, and SQLite FTS5 search over previous sessions.
- Native agent tools are named `memory_write`, `memory_read`, and
  `session_recall`.
- Global memory defaults to `~/.athena-code/memory/entries.jsonl`.
- Project memory defaults to `<project>/.context-workspace/memory/`.
- The project session index defaults to
  `<project>/.context-workspace/context/sessions.db`.
- Native memory is local-first; configured model providers still receive model
  requests through the underlying OpenCode provider system.
- The current packaged target is Linux x86_64.
- The project is MIT licensed.

## Primary documentation

- Overview and installation: README.md
- Development guide: CONTRIBUTING.md
- Security policy: SECURITY.md
- Memory design: docs/athena-turn-ownership-design.md
- Upstream attribution: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md

## Build model

The repository pins an OpenCode commit, applies
`patches/opencode-branding.patch`, copies Athena-owned files from `overlay/`,
and builds `runtime-bin/linux-x64/athena-code` with `scripts/build.sh`.

## Preferred terminology

Use "Athena Code" for the project and `athena-code` for the executable. Describe
it as an "open-source AI coding agent with persistent memory" or a
"memory-focused OpenCode fork."
